item.title: Darius Khondji On ‘Marty Supreme,’ Reuniting With Josh Safdie, Letting Timothée Chalamet Dance With The Light, and ‘Se7en’ [Interview]
item.description: Few cinematographers working today have a resumé as varied, influential, and quietly adventurous as Darius Khondji. From the moody, rain-soaked, bleach-bypassed nihilism of “Se7en” to the operatic stylization of “Delicatessen,” from the tactile, nerve-wracking intimacy of “Uncut Gems” to the genre-bending worlds of “Mickey 17” and “Eddington,” Khondji has built a career defined less by signature than by expanding curiosity. item.title: ‘The Choral’ Exclusive Clip: Ralph Fiennes Leads A WWI-Era Choir Drama About Grief, Survival, & Song
item.description: War stories usually sold you mud and heroics, but “The Choral” stayed home, in the places that had to keep breathing while the front line swallowed people whole. Set in 1916 Ramsden, Yorkshire, the film follows a Choral Society that has lost most of its men to the army, leaving the town to grapple with absence, dread, and the slow grind of conscription as World War I rages on the Western Front. item.description: A clinic in telling versus showing, there’s little left to the imagination in “Goodbye June” and even less that goes unsaid.
